focus: Angle 2: providers, models and the subscription
noveltyJustification: All eight findings are new: the two credential families, the declarative provider and model rows, the fetched model catalogue, reasoning as a model field rather than a flag, the Vibe Code budget counter, the plan-label mapping and the local cost record had no prior capture.
keyQuestions: How does Vibe run one task non-interactively: which prompt source, flags, output formats and exit codes does the headless contract expose?
Which providers, models and authentication paths can a Vibe dispatch use, and which usage counter does a turn draw on?
What does Vibe read from the working directory and ~/.vibe/, and what would a generated repo-root .vibe/ mirror contain?
For each cli-opencode surface this repository uses, does Vibe have an equivalent, a partial equivalent or none, and what would porting take?
What would a cli-mistral-vibe deep-loop executor kind need, and is ACP a better dispatch surface than print mode?
answeredQuestions: Which providers, models and authentication paths can a Vibe dispatch use, and which usage counter does a turn draw on?
ruledOut: Reading ~/.vibe/config.toml or a key to confirm the live provider: no config exists and key values are out of scope
Treating the model catalogue as a shipped roster: it is fetched from /model-catalog at runtime
